regions.text: Window = evidence density × rights maturity. Reassess when any signal moves: first AOC approval, filing density, same-entry follow-on payload, gaps filled in literature, rival head-to-head data

source: Source: IC Memo v2 (§3, §3.3–3.5, §4.1.7, App. D.2/D.4); ClinicalTrials.gov check of 33 assets (2026-10-11); data as of 2026-10-13
notes: Human readouts have lowered three risks, each with a clear reach: TfR1 delivery to skeletal muscle, splice correction in patient cells, and intrathecal oligo benefit in CNS. Phase 3 status, priority reviews and the Novartis–Avidity deal reduce feasibility and regulatory risk but provide no step-by-step delivery data. The window cannot be dated, but its closing signals can be monitored quarterly (order of magnitude, not rate). NewCo's response is to secure payload-sequence and disease-use rights now and generate its own transfection-free readouts for the first two payloads via the freedom-to-operate & backbone study (Rights & backbone-chemistry gate) and the productive-delivery study (Receptor-entry & payload-fit gate); the independent DYSF functional readout comes from the second-payload (DYSF) study (Platform-transfer gate). Cut for space: registry reads exclude trial results; del-desiran, del-brax and AOC 1044 lack animal tissue data in the materials.

notes: Each column has its own unit and denominator: assets (33 representative assets), patent publication numbers (60 core AOC), and disease/genotype records (94, of which 31 mechanism-verifiable), so no two columns can be summed. Late-stage assets are concentrated in a single system, skeletal muscle, while the most records sit in CNS: where activity is densest is not where assets are most advanced. Coverage is representative, not global; gaps are triaged as not captured, not found this round, or entry conditions not yet met. 'Approved' requires a company announcement plus registry confirmation; Phase 1 includes Phase 1/2. CGB1001 is excluded.

regions.text: A strong binder, a differentially expressed gene or an in vitro active sequence is not a usable AOC; best training data: one candidate in diseased vs normal cells, failures kept

source: Source: IC Memo v2 (§4.4); team analysis
notes: The seven application areas from the research are consolidated for NewCo into four task classes that wet-lab work can correct, each with its own validation loop and the same pass criterion. Maturity grades are a research judgement, not recorded facts. What AI cannot yet replace is functional-delivery validation: receptor-dependent productive intracellular payload and sequence-specific PD without transfection. The most valuable training data are uptake, productive payload, PD, function, toxicity and manufacturability for the same candidate in diseased and normal cells, including failed candidates. Cut for space: the seven acceptance criteria and four label-discipline rules are in the memo.

title: WuXi's internal AI evidence shows tools and a discovery workflow; the gain must come from a prospective blinded test

regions.heading: Design–test loop with three data boundaries

steps.heading: 1. Data & labels
steps.body: In-house training set; dosing conditions labelled; negatives stored on equal terms

steps.heading: 2. Design & ranking
steps.body: Rule/ML/generative design; objective = functional delivery; non-AI baseline run in parallel. Training set closes here

steps.heading: 3. Paired synthesis
steps.body: Fixed synthesis budget; equal numbers in AI and baseline arms; same payload and linker

steps.heading: 4. Wet-lab readout
steps.body: Transfection-free uptake; sorted target-cell PD; splice rescue, enzyme activity. Blind set sealed by patient/variant/batch, held by NewCo

steps.heading: 5. Blind-test read
steps.body: Held-out targets/donors; predefined endpoints; rounds and unit cost recorded

steps.heading: 6. Independent validation
steps.body: New donors, batches and executing party; third-party or internal replication; transferable raw data. Failures loop back to step 1

source: Source: IC Memo v2 (§4.4); blinded-testing and controls analysis; WuXi seminar photos (2026-10-29); data as of 2026-10-13
notes: WuXi's internal material supports 'tools exist and a payload-discovery workflow exists'; it does not yet quantify AI gain. That number should come from one prospective comparison on a defined target: the AI arm versus a reasonable non-AI baseline at the same experimental budget and task, recording cost per success, rounds needed, reproducibility and off-target effects. Labels from transfected conditions are tagged separately; galectin signals, homogenate means and tissue concentration are reference only, with positive labels taken from cell-resolved readouts. The ATXN2 hit rate is recorded as disclosed and under transfection, not as a validated AI gain. Next steps: answers to twelve questions for Andy Ng and the oligo discovery platform team, and a prospective-collaboration SOW (TBD).
